LESSON: WORD FORMATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.3: Word formation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Word formation, part of Reading in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: What do we need to do in order to read words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify syllables and sounds in preparation for reading words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Word formation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. blend syllables and sounds to form three letter words in and out of school,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Word formation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. read three letter words in and out of school,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Word formation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. perform activities that involve reading of three letter words in and out of school. • Listen to audio clips on word formation where syllables and sounds are joined and read out, ● Read sounds and syllables from charts, books and other materials. Learners with speech difficulties could point at the syllables on a chart, book or other materials as they listen to recorded ones. ● Blend syllables and sounds to form three words orally, example ca +t =cat pe+g =peg po + t =pot ● Read three letter words. Learner with speech difficulties could identify the three letter words from a chart as others read or read from an audio book or digital devices, ● Practises reading three letter words collaboratively. Learners with speech difficulties could read from audiobooks or appropriate digital devices, What do we need to do in order to read words? 90 ● Play games in forming three letter words. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use flash cards with tapes to form words. ● Learner gets involved in a variety of activities to read three letter words.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Word formation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Integrity: The learner without seeking assistance forms 3 letter words.

• Social justice: The learner practices equity by allowing each other an opportunity to read sounds and syllables from charts,

books and other materials.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify syllables and sounds in preparation for reading words,
2. blend syllables and sounds to form three letter words in and out of school,
3. read three letter words in and out of school,
4. perform activities that involve reading of three letter words in and out of school. • Listen to audio clips on word formation where syllables and sounds are joined and read out, ● Read sounds and syllables from charts, books and other materials. Core Competencies:

• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner reasons on how to join syllables and letter sounds to form 3 letter

words.

• Self-efficacy: The learner boldly plays games in forming three letter words.

Values:

• Integrity: The learner without seeking assistance forms 3 letter words.

• Social justice: The learner practices equity by allowing each other an opportunity to read sounds and syllables from charts,

books and other materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issue(
s) :

Social cohesion: The learner learns to work amicably with others and avoid conflicts even as they practice reading three letter

words.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Word formation is a prerequisite for reading and writing and so cuts across all the other Activity Areas in the curriculum.

Suggested learning resources: Book, audio books shelves, bags, tables, charts on letter sounds, flash cards, adapted digital

devices page turners.
